correctness.rationale: In exact integer arithmetic, the four overlap matrices Q_0..Q_3 are enumerated from 24,120,720,5040 permutations; the 24-by-24 asymptotic covariance has scale L=20160. The leading 18-by-18 integer principal minor has determinant nonzero modulo 1000003 (value 897856), proving rank >=18. Exact multiplication gives a 6-dimensional kernel of endpoint-coboundary vectors, proving rank <=18. The telescoping identity and boundary variance follow for every n, and the Gaussian limit follows by 3-dependence and Cramer–Wold. Bundled checker independently validates every matrix entry, rank, and 2304 finite covariance comparisons for orders 4 through 7. The finite checks alone do not establish the CLT.

originality.rationale: The complete rank-18/nullity-six kernel for all twenty-four length-four consecutive indicators is distinguished from already known single-pattern CLTs, lower-length contrasts, general overlap formulas, and unconstrained subsequence statistics. The published 2021/2022 constrained-pattern paper explicitly leaves degenerate linear combinations open in Remark 14.2; the 2023 full text computes the length-three system and only two length-four contrasts. Exact search comparisons and incomplete-access risks are recorded. Searches alone are not asserted to prove novelty.

value.rationale: This is a natural complete classification of all asymptotically degenerate linear functionals of the first 24-category local order-pattern histogram: it resolves the dimension, isolates five nontrivial endpoint invariants, and proves there are no hidden cancellations among remaining contrasts. The resulting exact 18-dimensional Gaussian support matters for constructing nonsingular joint null calibration in ordinal-pattern tests. It is motivated by the stated gap for constrained-pattern degeneracy and by direct calls for length-four analysis; not merely a table lookup or a routine parameter substitution.
